currentContext.business: The Company manufactures sugar, industrial alcohol/ethanol and bagasse-based power from sugarcane crushed at its fourteen Uttar Pradesh plants, selling sugar through mill-wise and area-wise agents to household and institutional buyers, alcohol/ethanol to oil marketing companies for petrol blending, to industrial chemical/paint/ink users and to liquor companies, and surplus power to the Uttar Pradesh state grid while using most generation captively. The BRSR states business activity mix as Sugar 87.37%, Industrial Alcohol 10.23% and power based on bagasse 2.40% of turnover; bagasse is also sold to industrial units for paper and eco-ply board. The Chairman describes an intent to transform the Company from a sugar company with distillery operations into an integrated bio-energy and biorefinery enterprise.

Power (co-generation): Bagasse-based power (captive + surplus sold to UP state grid)
By-products: Bagasse (sold to paper and eco-ply board units)

currentContext.expansion: The routed text discloses NO new company capex project with a commissioning or ramp timeline. Capacity is described as already installed and unchanged: fourteen sugar plants with aggregate crushing capacity of 1,36,000 TCD, six distilleries with aggregate industrial-alcohol capacity of 800 kilolitres per day, and fourteen co-generation plants with total power generation capacity of 449 MW (Board's Report, year ended March 31, 2026). The MD&A section 'BAJAJ HINDUSTHAN SUGAR'S (BHSL) POSITION' repeats 14 sugar plants at 136000 TCD and 6 distilleries at 800 KL/day but states 'about 151 MW of surplus power' — a different metric from the 449 MW total co-generation capacity given in the Board's Report and the Chairman's letter; both are recorded separately below rather than reconciled. The 14 mills are evenly spread across Uttar Pradesh — 5 in Western UP (48,000 TCD), 5 in Central UP (48,000 TCD) and 4 in Eastern UP (40,000 TCD) — with named Central-UP mills Barkhera, Maqsoodapur, Gola, Palia and Khambarkhera appearing only in the market-coverage prose; no per-mill capacity is printed. (Back-fill from the sibling profile bundle's BRSR Section A: all 14 plants are located in Uttar Pradesh and there are 3 offices — Mumbai, Noida and Lucknow; that BRSR table was not routed into this capex bundle.) Forward capacity intent is limited to the Chairman's imperatives: scaling ethanol production 'through multi-feedstock flexibility and capacity investment' and pursuing steam saving modules, flex-fuel, SAF and Iso-butanol opportunities — no project, size, cost or date attached. The MD&A de-risking paragraph states 'we are rapidly de-risking our business with the investment in power generation capacity', again without a project or timeline, and adds that although B-heavy/syrup diversion to ethanol began in Sugar Year 2020-21, current B-heavy and syrup ethanol prices are unviable so the Company 'kept not diverted any sugar towards Ethanol during last 2 years'. Cane development is described as a continuing investment ('continually investing in cane variety development', 'major thrust of the group on cane development'). Industry-level expansion context supplied in the MD&A (not company projects): oil companies' September-2021 dedicated-ethanol-plant scheme offering guaranteed lifting for time-bound new distilleries; ethanol movement by rail rakes/pipeline started at Mathura, Panipat and Kanpur depots; eased tender conditions (security/penalty cut from 5% to 1% from ethanol year 2020-21, then raised from 1% to 3% since ethanol year 2022-23); OMC payment cycle down to ~30 days from 35-40 days with a stated expectation of 21 days; and 20% ethanol blending with 95 RON becoming a mandatory norm for petrol nationwide with effect from 1st April 2026. BRSR Principle 2 records a STATED NIL: R&D 0.00% and Capex 0.00% of total R&D/capex invested in specific technologies to improve environmental and social impacts, in both the current and previous financial year. NAMED DISCLOSURE DEFECT — the '=== NAMED DISCLOSURE — CAPITAL COMMITMENTS ===' block supplied with this bundle carries neither readable column dates nor a unit line, so no figure from it is usable and capex_disclosed is returned empty. The block is reproduced verbatim: '[page 303] Year ended | As at / Estimated amount of contracts remaining to be executed on capital account and not provided for (net of advances). / 0.24 / 8.01'. The two bare numbers (0.24 and 8.01) cannot be assigned to a period or a unit (Rs crore vs Rs lakhs is not stated) and are therefore not extracted. currentContext.mdna: Indian sugar output has fallen for two consecutive years (2024-25 and 2025-26) on weather-related issues in Maharashtra and Karnataka and cane-variety issues in Uttar Pradesh; in these two years gross production exceeded consumption but net production (after diversion to ethanol) was below consumption.|Industry-wide, management flags lower cane availability, underutilisation of sugar plant capacity, lower sugar recovery, no increase in sugar MSP, no increase in ethanol prices and non-availability of adequate ethanol orders resulting in underutilisation of distillery capacity.|All-India gross sugar production peaked at 39.0 million mt in 2021-22 and has declined continuously since; 2024-25 gross was a five-year low 29.6 million mt (net 26.1 million mt); 2025-26 gross is estimated at 30.9 million mt (+4.4%) with net production around 27.8 million mt, far below the initial 34-35 million mt estimates (a 10%+ deviation from ISMA's initial 34.3 million mt estimate).|Closing sugar stocks for 2025-26 are estimated at an all-time low 4.1 million mt, 14.6% of domestic consumption, easing inventory carrying cost and quality-deterioration burden; despite low stocks the report notes adequate market availability and no abnormal price surge.|Exports remain restricted to Government quotas: nil quota in 2023-24, 1.0 million mt in 2024-25, and 2.0 million mt for 2025-26 (1.5 million mt pro-rata to all mills plus 0.5 million mt to willing mills) — but only about 0.7 million mt is estimated to actually be exported, on five-year-low international prices and logistics bottlenecks from the Middle East conflict; major exports were low-quality white (sulphitation) sugar helped by a strong USD and regional FOB premiums.|Sugar MSP has been unchanged at Rs 3,100 per qtl since 2019 while cane FRP rose 29.5% from Rs 275 to Rs 365 per qtl (10.25% recovery basis) for 2026-27 and UP SAP (early variety) rose 23.1% from Rs 325 to Rs 400 per qtl; sugar prices continue to prevail below production costs and fall to alarmingly low levels during the crushing season. Media reports suggest the Government was considering an MSP increase to Rs 3,800 per qtl, but a favourable decision is awaited; the industry is also seeking automatic indexation of MSP to cane price.|Ethanol economics are the key margin swing factor: 2025-26 is the third consecutive year without a Government price increase for B-heavy and sugar-syrup based ethanol, making current ethanol prices unviable against cost, so many mills — particularly in UP — are prioritising sugar production and keeping ethanol capacity idle.|Ethanol allocation shortfall: in 2025-26 cycle-I the industry received orders for 288.5 crore litres through the sugar route against bids of 472 crore litres (61.1%), versus 311.9 crore litres against 391.3 crore bid (79.7%) in 2024-25 cycle-I, after which no further tender cycle was floated for B-heavy/syrup ethanol — a clear case of oversupply and surplus distillation capacity.|Demand-side policy levers management points to: raising blending beyond 20%, flexi-fuel vehicles taking E85/E100, ethanol cooking stoves, ethanol blending with diesel, and Sustainable Aviation Fuel — supported by import-substitution and forex-savings arguments amid the Middle East conflict.|Weather outlook: 2026 is estimated to be an El-Nino year with monsoon below normal at 90-95% of Long Period Average, which may affect the 2026-27 crop and also sowing for the 2027-28 season; however, since 2024 and 2025 were normal monsoon years there is no indication of a production shortfall for 2026-27.|USDA estimates a 12% increase in Indian sugar production (raw value) from 30.0 million mt to 33.6 million mt in 2026-27; other analysts peg 2026-27 higher by 1.0-1.5 million mt versus last year.|World sugar balance (ISO, updated Feb 2026, Oct-Sept year): 2025-26 production 181.29 million mt against consumption 180.07 million mt — a surplus of 1.22 million mt versus a deficit of 3.46 million mt in 2024-25; end stocks 93.30 million mt and stocks/consumption 51.81%.|For 2026-27 third-party views diverge: Green Pool raised its global deficit estimate to 4.30 million mt from 1.66 million mt citing a shift to higher ethanol production at the expense of sugar, while Covrig Analytics cut its surplus estimate to 800,000 MT from 1.4 million mt.|Brazil Centre-South (UNICA, April-March): 2025-26 cane crush fell 1.7% to 611.15 million mt while sugar production rose 0.6% to 40.43 million mt on higher diversion to sugar (average 50.38%, having run up to 54% in the first half before weak sugar prices and better ethanol parity pulled it down); ethanol production 33.72 billion litres and TRS 137.79; diversion of cane towards sugar is estimated to come down during 2026-27.|Thailand (USDA): sugar production rose almost 10% to 11.26 million mt in 2025/26 and is estimated to fall 15.6% to 9.50 million mt, with exports easing to 6.0 million mt from 7.0 million mt (the narrative dates this decline as '2025-2026' while the table places the 9.50/6.00 figures under the 2026-2027 column — the mismatch is reproduced as printed).|Crude oil (Brent) — a major macro driver of sugar prices and of Brazilian cane diversion to ethanol — opened at USD 74.49/bbl on 1 April 2025, touched a low of USD 58.92/bbl in December 2025 and stood at USD 118.35/bbl on 31 March 2026, with extreme volatility from February 2026 on the start of the Middle East conflict.|Currency: the Brazilian real moved from 5.68 in early April 2025 to a high of 6.01, a low of 5.13 in February 2026, closing at 5.18; the Indian rupee depreciated 9.2% from 85.6 to 93.5 per USD (strongest 84.3, weakest 94.8) — the chart narrative labels this period '2024-25' while quoting 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026 dates.|Company-level tailwinds cited by the Chairman: continued improvements in ethanol realisations, healthier sugar inventories and strengthening industry fundamentals reinforce the attractiveness of the integrated business model; the restructured capital structure substantially reduces near-term debt servicing obligations.|Structural remedies management calls for: better cane varieties, use of Artificial Intelligence for improved cane productivity, and water conservation mechanisms such as drip irrigation, rainwater harvesting, trash shedding and mulching to address volatility in sugar production, declining productivity and recovery, cane varietal issues and weather vagaries.|No company-level order book is disclosed. The only order/allocation pipeline discussed is industry-wide ethanol tendering: in 2025-26 cycle-I the industry received orders for 288.5 crore litres of ethanol through the sugar route against bids of 472 crore litres (61.1% of bid quantity); in 2024-25 cycle-I, orders of 311.9 crore litres were placed against bids of 391.3 crore litres (79.7%), after which no further tender cycle was floated by the oil companies for B-heavy molasses / syrup ethanol.|Sugar export entitlement is quota-based rather than order-book based: for 2025-26 the Government allowed a 2.0 million mt export quota (1.5 million mt to all mills in proportion to production plus 0.5 million mt to willing mills), against which only about 0.7 million mt is estimated to be exported.

risks.risk: Cane availability, cane variety and recovery (raw material risk)
risks.note: MD&A 'Key risks and concerns' item 1: in Uttar Pradesh the cane variety issue has had 'serious implications on cane yield and sugar recovery in last 2-3 years'. Cane is the single input (BRSR: sugarcane is about 90% of total inputs, sourced from local farmers), so yield/recovery loss feeds straight through to sugar, ethanol and cogen volumes. Mitigation stated is continual investment in cane quality promotion and variety development. A second, self-inflicted leg is flagged explicitly: 'the ability to make timely cane price payments to farmers which is affecting the availability of cane to Group' — cane dues are both a liquidity and a supply problem.

risks.risk: Sugar price risk — administered cane cost against market-determined sugar realisation, with MSP frozen since 2019
risks.note: MD&A item 2: cane prices are fixed by the state government while sugar realisations are wholly market-driven, which 'at times led to a complete mismatch'. The Minimum Selling Price of Rs 31.0 per kg was fixed in February 2019 and has not been raised in the seven years since, while cane FRP rose 29.5%; industry associations are lobbying for Rs 40-42 per kg and for MSP to be indexed to cane price. Management states MSP increase 'is urgently required to prevent sugar price fall during sugar surplus situations / during peak of crushing season'.

MD&A item 3: 'The biggest risk to the business is the disjointed sugarcane price fixed by the state government', alongside environmental, raw-material-pricing and general policy risk. The offsetting factor stated is continuing Central and State policy and subsidy support to enable mills to pay the fixed cane price — i.e. viability depends on policy decisions (export quotas, ethanol allocations, diversion permissions, subsidy release) rather than on the Company's own actions. The Board's Report separately cites 'non-settlement of subsidy claims under the Sugar Promotion Policy of Uttar Pradesh government' as a cause of the cash-flow mismatch (provenance: sibling capex_expansion / strategy_outlook bundles).

risks.risk: Ethanol economics — unviable B-heavy/syrup prices and inadequate offtake leaving distillery capacity idle
risks.note: The de-risking strategy is explicitly not working at current prices: although diversion of sugar to ethanol via B-heavy molasses/sugar syrup began in Sugar Year 2020-21, 'as current Ethanol prices from B Heavy and Syrup Ethanol are not viable, we kept not diverted any sugar towards Ethanol during last 2 years'. Ethanol prices from the sugar route have not been raised for three years and the industry received only 61.1% of its bid quantity in the 2025-26 cycle-I tender (provenance for the tender and price detail: sibling strategy_outlook / capex_expansion bundles). This strands a large part of the 800 KL/day distillery platform.

risks.risk: Single-state, single-crop geographic and asset concentration
risks.note: All 14 plants are located in Uttar Pradesh with zero international plants or offices (BRSR item 18), the Company processes nearly 12% of UP's sugarcane, and there are no direct exports (BRSR item 19 prints '-' for number of international countries served — a stated nil, with refined sugar reaching export markets only indirectly via merchant exporters against a Government-issued quota). A UP-specific weather, cane-disease, variety or state-policy shock hits the entire asset base at once. Market share is also eroding: BHSL net sugar production fell to 1.03 million MT (2025-26 estimate) from 1.94 million MT in 2019-20, and its share of UP production slipped from 15.35% (2019-20) to 11.48% (2025-26E) and of All-India from 7.08% to 3.71%.

risks.risk: Balance-sheet stress and dependence on the lender Resolution Plan
risks.note: The Company entered a restructuring under the RBI Prudential Framework after a prolonged mismatch between cane procurement cost and flat sugar realisations left it unable to service principal and interest; two of the eight board seats are lender nominee directors (Punjab National Bank and State Bank of India). Continued compliance depends on a Rs 1,000 crore promoter/Company infusion, a minimum Rs 150 crore of non-core asset sales within two years, and a Bajaj Energy shortfall guarantee for any EBITDA/capex shortfall until FY2032 — with security including promoter personal guarantee and pledges of 31,87,43,422 promoter shares (provenance: sibling strategy_outlook bundle; the restructuring text was not routed into this risks bundle). Loss-making subsidiaries (notably Phenil Sugars Limited, which recorded a loss after tax in both FY2025-26 and FY2024-25 — figures deliberately not reproduced) add to the drag.

BRSR material-issue table rows 1 and 2, both classed as Risks with negative financial implications. Climate: 'Variations in rainfall patterns, temperatures, and extreme weather events directly affect crop yields and quality', plus regulatory and reputational risk from rising GHG emissions; mitigated by climate-resilient crop varieties, efficient irrigation and alternative energy. Water: sugar manufacture is water-intensive and 'water scarcity and pollution can profoundly impact the company's functioning, leading to disruptions in the supply chain and increased operational costs'; mitigated by Zero Liquid Discharge across distilleries and reuse of treated sugar effluent.

risks.risk: Workforce health and safety in a labour-intensive operation
risks.note: BRSR material-issue row 7 (Risk, negative): the workforce faces occupational hazards including falls, transportation-related incidents, equipment malfunctions and heat stress, and 'non-compliance with safety standards can lead to significant regulatory penalties, reputational damage, and the potential loss of skilled labour'. The Company employs 7,146 people as at March 31, 2026, of whom 4,241 workers are other-than-permanent — a largely seasonal, contract workforce. Mitigation is HIRA and JSA risk assessment, regular safety inspections, third-party and internal cross-functional audits and safety training.

Sales are routed overwhelmingly through a small dealer/distributor set: 86.37% of total sales went to dealers/distributors in FY2025-26 (82.11% in FY2024-25) across just 34 dealers (29 prior year), with the top 10 accounting for 71.42% of dealer sales (68.86% prior year) — a structural counterparty concentration even though the AR does not label it a risk (provenance: BRSR Principle 1 'Openness of business' table, routed into the sibling capex_expansion bundle, not into this one). Institutional demand is being built with named buyers including Pepsi (Varun Beverages), Wrigley, Walmart, ITC, Dabur, Hamdard, Reliance and Udaan, supported by FSSC 22000 licences at four units.

Beyond UP, the Company competes with mills in Maharashtra, Karnataka, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu, and in the neighbouring markets of Punjab, Haryana and Bihar with local mills. 'Sugar sales market reach / penetration is purely based on the price parity and Quality with competing mills' — and an increasing number of mills are converting from sulphitation sugar to refined sugar, giving better-quality producers an edge on colour (ICUMSA), grain size and lustre. Offsetting stated fact: 'Since Sugar imports are not viable and not happening there is no competition from Imported Sugar' — a stated absence of import competition.

risks.risk: Land use, labour rights and ethical-conduct exposure
risks.note: BRSR material-issue rows 3, 4 and 5, all classed as Risks with negative financial implications: sugar production's substantial land footprint can contribute to deforestation, land degradation and biodiversity loss with reputational and regulatory consequences; labour practices and supply-chain management carry risk of labour-rights violations and substandard working conditions; and corruption or bribery would damage reputation and create legal risk. Mitigations stated are agroforestry and reforestation, biodiversity collaboration, strengthened labour policies with audits and grievance mechanisms, and anti-corruption policies with partner due diligence and ethics training.

themes.title: Bioenergy / Ethanol / SAF transition
themes.need: Higher ethanol-blending mandates (E20->E25/E27/E30), CBG, SAF and bio-IBA underpin a multi-year bioenergy capex cycle. PRAJIND's near-term earnings are depressed by a 1G slowdown + GenX gestation but the optionality (SAF, CBG, DC-cooling) is large; TRUALT/BALRAMCHIN/EIDPARRY/TRIVENI/GODAVARIB add ethanol/sugar; BCLIND/GULPOLY/GLOBUSSPR on grain-based distillation.
themes.driver: Higher blending-mandate notifications; SAF/CBG order conversion; sugar-cycle realisations.
